items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic released its next frontier model in two access tiers, Fable (general availability) and Mythos (restricted to vetted organizations), claiming up to 30% faster generation and stronger agentic-coding and cybersecurity benchmark scores than the 5.1 models. It's the company's first frontier launch since CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the pace of AI development, and comes days before Anthropic's IPO roadshow wraps up.

items.headline: Anthropic sets terms for Nasdaq IPO, targets trading debut this week
items.summary: Anthropic is offering 825 million shares at an expected $70-$78 each, seeking up to $64.4 billion in proceeds at a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation, with pricing expected November 18 and trading set to begin November 19 on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Seven of its chip and cloud suppliers have also agreed to buy $26 billion of shares in a private placement alongside the public offering.

items.headline: LangChain raises $300M at $3B valuation, led by Alphabet's CapitalG
items.summary: The AI agent-tooling startup more than doubled its valuation in just over a year, with the new funding earmarked for expanding LangSmith, its platform for evaluating, monitoring and deploying enterprise AI agents. The round underscores continued investor appetite for the 'agent infrastructure' layer sitting between foundation models and production applications.

items.headline: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 for cell-specific DNA predictions
items.summary: The genomics model, trained on more than 100 million cell profiles across 68 tissues, predicts how a given DNA variant behaves in a specific cell type or state rather than as a tissue-wide average, roughly doubling detection of causal variants on an immune-cell benchmark. It's free for non-commercial research via DeepMind's API, with commercial access in private preview.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini Decisions API for fast, fixed-menu AI calls
items.summary: Built on a new 'Gemini Decision 1' model, the API answers up to 1,000 structured multiple-choice-style questions in a single call across text, image, audio, video and PDF inputs, aimed at cheaper, lower-latency agent workflows than open-ended generation. Google says it's already using the model internally to route queries between model tiers in Gemini Notebook.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen becomes the default model in Google's AI Mode
items.summary: Google rolled its faster, cheaper Gemini 4 Hydrogen model out to every Search user and made it the default for AI Mode worldwide, positioning it as the speed-focused tier beneath the more reasoning-heavy Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon models. The swap replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as the workhorse model behind AI Overviews and AI Mode's hardest queries.

items.headline: AI-training data startup Mercor raises $750M at a $20B valuation
items.summary: The round, backed by Nvidia, Salesforce and Zoom among others, doubles Mercor's valuation from its October 2025 Series C just over a year ago. The company matches skilled contractors to AI labs for model training and evaluation data, and its rapid growth is closely tied to spending from the largest frontier AI developers.

items.headline: Baidu open-sources ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, a 280B-parameter MoE model
items.summary: The mixture-of-experts model has 280 billion total parameters but only 14 billion active per token, and was pre-trained on 33.5 trillion tokens; Baidu published FP8 and BF16 weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope under a license that's free for commercial use up to $50 million in related annual revenue. It's one of China's largest open-weight releases this year as domestic labs race to match frontier Western models.

items.headline: US lawmakers push for tighter AI chip export controls on China
items.summary: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks issued a joint statement demanding stronger restrictions, alleging Nvidia received approvals to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, as reports surface of a possible new rule targeting Chinese firms' remote access to AI chips hosted in third-country data centers. The push follows earlier Commerce Department guidance closing a loophole for China-headquartered firms operating abroad.

items.headline: Microsoft Ignite 2026 opens in San Francisco with agentic AI as centerpiece
items.summary: Satya Nadella and Judson Althoff kicked off the four-day conference with a keynote expected to focus on tools for building, governing and securing autonomous AI agents across the Microsoft 365 and Azure stack, building on last year's Agent 365 launch. The event runs through November 20 and typically sets Microsoft's enterprise AI direction for the following year.

items.headline: Unitree details 'Physical AI Robot Self-Evolution' system for humanoids
items.summary: Founder Wang Xingxing unveiled a framework, dubbed internally as Self-Evolution V1.0, in which an AI system searches research papers, writes code and tests it in simulation before running trials on physical robots, aiming to let humanoids improve their own skills with less manual engineering. The company has so far disclosed only the technical approach, with no published benchmarks or real-world success rates yet.
